trigger_condition: _guard_blocked_gate reads only _gate_status_target, so a whole-node gate replacement with status=passed is never checked.
guard_snippet: Drive _guard_blocked_gate from _written_gate(path, value) and resolve the current node for both scalar and node writes, as _guard_reopen already does.
potential_consequence: A gate blocked on missing evidence is recorded passed through the documented --replace form, with validate clean and override_reason null.

trigger_condition: The dotted-ticket-id rejection is inside the `if "gates" in parts` branch, so tickets.<dotted-id>.<field> and whole-node paths still reach get_parent and create a phantom nested ticket.
guard_snippet: Reject a dotted id for every tickets.<id>... path, not only gate paths; compare the id prefix against the exact keys in the ticket map.
potential_consequence: set exits 0; validate then errors 'tickets.1.gates must be a mapping', and only a hand edit repairs it.

trigger_condition: done refuses when ledger_tickets is non-empty and project_root is None before the accept-missing-tickets branch, so a custom-ledger close cannot use the documented escape hatch.
guard_snippet: Compute artifact_tickets as None when project_root is None, then guard once on `ledger_tickets and artifact_tickets is None` with --accept-missing-tickets --reason; mention --project-root only as a hint.
potential_consequence: A workstream whose ledger is not at the default path can never close, and the refusal text hides the documented escape.

trigger_condition: _guard_reopen checks later ticket gates but never the workstream state, so a ticket gate can reopen after the workstream is done.
guard_snippet: Refuse a reopen when workstream.status == 'done' (or reopen the workstream/phase in the same write), mirroring the phase check.
potential_consequence: ticket returns ok, validate then reports 'done with undecided gates', and summary leaves next_action null.

trigger_condition: _guard_reopen keys on status == 'open' only, so a decided gate can be demoted to blocked with no reason; override_reason is cleared and decided_at is stamped.
guard_snippet: Treat every transition out of passed|overridden|skipped as a reopen requiring --reason, and set decided_at only for a decided status.
potential_consequence: An audited override reason is erased with no reason or reopen record, and the gate becomes unpassable without an override.

trigger_condition: A gate-node replacement without a status is accepted; _validate_value only checks status when the replacement happens to contain one.
guard_snippet: Require isinstance(value, dict) with status in GATE_STATUSES for every gate-node write, and route the node through the scalar guards before writing.
potential_consequence: set reports success, the decided gate disappears, and validate then rejects the ledger.

trigger_condition: The new removal example writes a null node with --null --replace instead of deleting the key.
guard_snippet: Support deletion explicitly (set --delete, or ticket --delete --id), or document a working removal and add a test that validate is clean and the id is gone from summary.
potential_consequence: Following the reference produces 'tickets.<id> must be a mapping' and a ticket that can never be closed.

trigger_condition: done resolves --project-root raw; only --plan, --memlog, and --template go through expand_project_root, while SKILL.md:17 says the script expands {project-root}.
guard_snippet: Expand --project-root in every command that takes it, or scope the SKILL sentence to the flags that do and substitute at the call site.
potential_consequence: A conductor copying the documented line sees a false missing-evidence/ticket-artifact gap and may waive it.

trigger_condition: Reopening a decided phase (done/skipped -> active) needs no reason and logs none, while the gate guard's error tells the agent to do exactly that.
guard_snippet: Require --reason for a decided phase reopen and record it in the memlog; add the verb to the menu and gate-matrix.
potential_consequence: The documented remediation for a blocked gate reopen reverses a done phase without an audit reason.

trigger_condition: No menu verb, loop step, or gate-matrix subsection covers reopening a gate or phase; the rule exists only in a ledger-schema comment.
guard_snippet: Add a reopen row to menu.md and a 'Reopening' subsection to gate-matrix.md with the legal sequence and the later-gate/phase constraints.
potential_consequence: An agent that hits 'reopening a decided gate needs --reason' has no documented verb and will hand-edit the YAML or invent an invalid sequence.

trigger_condition: done does not check that --project-root is a directory, unlike detect/init at 1435 and 1443.
guard_snippet: Validate project_root.is_dir() and fail with the searched roots before the artifact checks.
potential_consequence: A typo is indistinguishable from genuinely missing evidence and invites an unnecessary acceptance waiver.

trigger_condition: The close note records the reason but never names the accepted gap or the stale tickets; both accept flags produce the same line.
guard_snippet: Append the accepted missing_evidence or stale_tickets list before the reason in close_note.
potential_consequence: A post-hoc reader cannot tell what was waived at close, which is the question the accept flags exist to answer.

trigger_condition: A hand-edited ledger mixes integer and string ticket ids; done subtracts and sorts the two types together.
guard_snippet: Normalize ledger_tickets = {str(t) for t in tickets} before the set math, the sort, and the join.
potential_consequence: done raises a TypeError on a legal hand-edited ledger and the workstream cannot close.

trigger_condition: set writes tickets.<dotted-id>.<field> when the path has no gates segment.
guard_snippet: Reject dotted ticket ids for every path under tickets, not only the gate-path branch.
potential_consequence: set exits 0; validate rejects the phantom ticket and only a hand edit repairs it.

trigger_condition: A ticket gate reopens after the workstream was closed with done.
guard_snippet: Refuse when root.status == 'done' before the phase/ticket branches, or reopen the workstream in the same write.
potential_consequence: The command returns ok; validate then rejects the done workstream as undecided.

trigger_condition: set replaces a blocked gate node with status passed via --replace.
guard_snippet: Gate on _written_gate(path, value)[3] == 'passed' and resolve the current node for scalar and node forms.
potential_consequence: The blocked gate is recorded passed with no override reason and validate stays clean.

trigger_condition: A decided gate is set to blocked; no command treats blocked as a decision change.
guard_snippet: Treat blocked like open in _guard_reopen and keep the existing override_reason when no --reason is supplied.
potential_consequence: An audited override reason is erased without a reason or reopen record.

trigger_condition: The new example removes a ticket by writing a null key.
guard_snippet: Make set --path tickets.<id> --null --replace delete the key, or replace the example with a supported removal.
potential_consequence: set returns ok, validate fails, and migrate does not repair the null ticket key.

trigger_condition: _guard_reopen's phase branch is never executed: no test writes a gates.<phase>.<gate> status to open.
guard_snippet: Add a phase variant to test_set_reopening_a_decided_gate_needs_a_reason: pass the plan gates, set phases.plan done, assert reopening gates.plan.requirements fails with 'reopen the phase first', then run validate.
potential_consequence: The branch can regress or be deleted as dead code while the suite stays green, and a phase gate reopens under a done phase.
consumer: set --path gates.<phase>.<gate>.status --value open, the only command that reopens a phase gate (ledger-schema.md:203-212).
evidence: grep of test_sdlc_plan.py for '"open"' returns 406, 752, 1803, 1818, 1835, 1842, 1869, 1882; all are ticket paths. A scratch run confirmed the guard fires and that validate would reject the ledger if it did not.

trigger_condition: The blocked->passed guard is only tested through .status writes; no test performs a node replacement.
guard_snippet: Block tickets.T1.gates.review, then assert set --path tickets.T1.gates.review --value '{"status":"passed"}' --replace --reason probe fails with 'a blocked gate cannot be passed'; repeat for a phase gate.
potential_consequence: The guard can be bypassed through the documented node-replacement form with validate clean; the ticket's grant of --reason is lost.
consumer: set --path tickets.<id>.gates.<gate> / gates.<phase>.<gate> whole-node replacement, documented at ledger-schema.md:266-267.
evidence: A scratch repro returned ok:true and summary status passed with override_reason null. Both existing blocked->passed tests (test_sdlc_plan.py:2249-2274 and 1734-1774) use the .status path; grep for 'blocked gate cannot be passed' returns only those two assertions.

trigger_condition: The done memlog test asserts only the substring 'marked done', which passes with or without the new reason suffix.
guard_snippet: Assert 'marked done (reason: memlog path fixture)' in the memlog test, and assert the reason in the accepted branch of test_done_refuses_tickets_without_a_ticket_artifact.
potential_consequence: Deleting the close-note reason leaves the suite green, so the audit claim in the r2 review and fix-progress ships unverified.
consumer: close.mark_done -> done --accept-missing-tickets --reason, advertised at sdlc_plan.py:3135-3138 and ledger-schema.md:233-239.
evidence: A scratch run emitted 'workstream ws-001 marked done (reason: ledger-only fixture)'. The only assertion on that line is test_sdlc_plan.py:1945 assertIn('marked done', ...); test_done_refuses_tickets_without_a_ticket_artifact asserts only accepted['ok'].

trigger_condition: The dotted-id guard is untested for paths without a gates segment, which is exactly where it is missing.
guard_snippet: Extend test_set_rejects_a_dotted_ticket_id with set --path tickets.1.3.note --value phantom --replace --reason probe -> ok:false with the ticket-command message.
potential_consequence: The corruption R5 was meant to end is still reachable, and the suite reports success.
consumer: set --path tickets.<dotted-id>.<field> and the whole-node form, the same surface as the documented ticket example at ledger-schema.md:203-205.
evidence: A scratch run returned ok:true and then validate reported 'tickets.1.gates must be a mapping'. The only dotted-id test (test_sdlc_plan.py:1888-1902) uses tickets.1.3.gates.review.status.

trigger_condition: The set reopen test never inspects the node; the ticket twin asserts override_reason is cleared, so only the set half is unpinned.
guard_snippet: After the accepted set reopen, assert summary tickets.items.T1.gates.ticket.override_reason is None, mirroring test_sdlc_plan.py:1843, and add the phase variant.
potential_consequence: A reopen reason written onto an open gate is later read as an override reason, so a required gate can be overridden without a supplied reason.
consumer: set --path tickets.<id>.gates.<gate>.status --value open --reason, then a later override write on the same node.
evidence: test_set_reopening_a_decided_gate_needs_a_reason (test_sdlc_plan.py:1845-1886) ends at assertTrue(accepted['ok']); the ticket test asserts override_reason at 1843.

trigger_condition: test_migrate_materializes_levels_and_tickets clears the map with set --path tickets --null --replace, which the script rejects; the test ignores the result.
guard_snippet: Replace the set call with self.edit_ledger("del data['workstreams']['ws-001']['tickets']") as the round-2 pass did at line 887, and assert the rebuilt map.
potential_consequence: The test named for migrate's ticket materialization runs against an intact map, so a regression that stops creating the map ships green.
consumer: sdlc_plan.py migrate on an older ledger with no workstreams.<id>.tickets map, documented at ledger-schema.md:243-245.
evidence: A scratch run of the exact setup call returned ok:false, 'unknown ticket path: tickets'. The test asserts only migrated['ok'], validate['ok'], and warnings == [], none of which distinguishes an empty map from a preserved one.
